dataset_name: ISIC 2024 / Historical: The International Skin Imaging Collaboration skin lesion analysis challenges

metadata.summary: The ISIC Archive and its annual challenges provide the largest publicly available collection of dermoscopic images of skin lesions for skin cancer analysis. ISIC 2024 (SLICE-3D) released 401,059 training images (crops from 3D total-body photography) from 1,042 patients for melanoma classification. Historical ISIC challenges (e.g., 2020) contributed 33,126 DICOM images and incorporated prior datasets including HAM10000.
metadata.purpose: Supporting skin cancer classification and segmentation research via annual academic challenges.

ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification performed per HIPAA Safe Harbor standards; facial and identifying features removed or obscured.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with GDPR and HIPAA de-identification requirements where applicable.

known_limitations: Underrepresentation of pediatric and elderly populations
Geographic bias toward high-resource countries with dermatology imaging infrastructure
Limited diversity in skin tone (Fitzpatrick I–IV overrepresented; V–VI underrepresented)
Label noise from clinical vs. histopathological diagnosis discordance
Temporal shift: older subsets (e.g., HAM10000) reflect earlier imaging protocols and diagnostic practices
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes — 2024 images are crops from 3D total-body photography; historical images underwent format conversion (e.g., DICOM to PNG), re-sampling, and label harmonization.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Predominantly North American and European institutions; Fitzpatrick skin types V–VI underrepresented.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Rare malignancies (e.g., Merkel cell carcinoma, dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans) severely underrepresented.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Performance may degrade on populations with darker skin tones, in low-resource settings, or with non-standard imaging devices.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Subgroup coverage by skin tone, age, sex, and geography is incompletely reported and likely uneven.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Age, sex, ethnicity, and Fitzpatrick scale metadata missing or inconsistently recorded across historical releases.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Direct clinical deployment without validation; use in commercial diagnostic products without explicit license amendment.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Images selected from international multi-site contributors for standardized skin lesion analysis challenges.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Multi-site, multi-institutional aggregation; historical inclusion of pre-existing datasets (e.g., HAM10000) with possible re-cropping and re-labeling per challenge protocol.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from international clinical sites and prior public datasets (e.g., HAM10000); 2024 data derived from 3D total-body photography crops.

population.target_population: Patients undergoing dermatologic evaluation for skin lesions, including melanoma and benign lesions.
population.inclusion_criteria: Skin lesion images acquired via dermoscopy or 3D total-body photography, meeting challenge-specific quality and annotation criteria.
population.exclusion_criteria: Images failing quality control or lacking diagnostic consensus labels per challenge protocol.
population.missing_groups: Pediatric and elderly populations underrepresented relative to general skin cancer epidemiology; no explicit reporting of age distribution or representation balance.

annotation.annotation_method: Expert dermatologist consensus labeling; some labels derived from clinical ground truth (e.g., biopsy-confirmed diagnosis).

annotators.qualifications: Board-certified dermatologists and skin imaging specialists

annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels sourced from clinical diagnosis (e.g., histopathology), expert consensus, or prior dataset annotations (e.g., HAM10000).
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise exists due to inter-observer variability, evolving diagnostic criteria, and reliance on non-biopsy clinical diagnoses in some subsets.
